The Earth is clearly round when viewed from space. The horizon curves, and this can be measured. The sun rises and sets as the Earth rotates. If the Earth is flat, then why does the sun disappear from the sky every night? If the Earth is flat, why has no one found its "edge?" Why is gravity uniform across the Earth's surface? Different constellations are visible from different points on the Earth. If the Earth was flat, then we'd all have more-or-less the same view of the same constellations. You can see more from higher up, and this shows that the Earth has curvature. How can planes and ships circumnavigate the globe if it is flat? Why would the Earth be flat if other planets are round?
If you even have to debate this I suggest you to get acquainted with a better crowd.

There's a jillion ways to prove the Earth is round, but here's one of the simplest: When you're sailing, and you see a ship approaching on the horizon, you don't see the whole ship. First, you just see the highest point of the ship, like the mast if it's a sailboat. This occurs because the curved surface of the water blocks the rest. As the ship gets closer, the rest of it appears.

Another one that comes to my mind involves the propagation of radio waves at VHF and above, where line-of-sight propagation dominates. Radio stations get weaker as your distance from the transmitter increases according to the inverse-square law, but in real life, propagation is somewhat worse than LOS due to multipath interference (when the signal bounces off objects as it travels, and your antenna receives multiple copies of the signal that can subtract in phase) and obstructions like trees, buildings, hills etc. But once you get past 60 miles or so, the signal strength drops rapidly since the Earth's curvature blocks the line-of-sight signal. To some extent, signals get bent downwards by the atmosphere or diffract off the horizon, but once you get far away enough, the Earth's curvature becomes an insurmountable obstacle and the signal fades into noise. If the Earth was flat, signals could travel in a straight line between any two points on Earth, with only the gradual dispersion over distance and the occasional mountain range to attenuate them, and you'd receive strong FM and TV signals from hundreds (even thousands?) of miles away.
